title: Tile Removal Sarasota FL | Dust-Controlled Floor Demo
description: Tile removal in Sarasota and Manatee County: dust-controlled demo with HEPA vacuum shrouds, $2.50-$4.50 per sq ft for glued tile with thinset chip-out, 2026.
h1: Dust-Controlled Tile and Flooring Removal in Sarasota and Manatee County
lede: Tile removal is usually the first job on the schedule, not the last, because almost nothing else in a flooring project can start until the old surface and its mortar bed are out and the slab underneath has been checked.
capsule: Tile removal in Sarasota and Manatee County runs $1.75 to $3.25 per square foot for carpet, laminate or floating floors and $2.50 to $4.50 per square foot for glued tile with thinset chip-out, in 2026. We run chipping hammers and grinders through a HEPA vacuum shroud to cut dust, though no demo method removes all of it. Heavier mortar beds and mastic add to the price.

sections.h2: What does dust-controlled tile removal actually mean?
sections.html:
Dust-controlled removal routes the chipping hammer, floor scraper and thinset grinder through a HEPA-filtered vacuum shroud, so debris and fine dust get pulled into a canister at the point of impact instead of filling the room. We seal doorways with plastic and run a negative-air machine to keep dust from migrating into the rest of the house while the crew works. That combination cuts airborne dust by a wide margin compared with an open jackhammer-and-broom approach, but breaking a mortar bed or grinding old thinset off a slab still throws some dust into the air; nobody can promise a completely dust-free demo.

Homeowners searching for dustless tile removal near me are really asking for that HEPA-shroud-and-containment approach, since old tile, thinset and grout can carry silica dust that's worth minimizing rather than ignoring. We treat dust control as standard practice on every removal job, not an upsell. Crews wear respirators rated for fine mineral dust regardless of how well the containment is working, and on a whole-house job we run the negative-air machine through a window or exterior door so the pressure differential actually pulls air out of the work zone instead of just filtering what's already inside it. Broken tile and mortar go straight into contractor bags or a driveway dumpster rather than piling up inside the house, which keeps foot traffic through the rest of the home to a minimum while demo is underway.

sections.h2: Do you always have to remove the old tile first?
sections.html:
Not always. Some rigid-core vinyl plank lines, including COREtec's, can be installed over an existing hard surface as long as it's fully adhered, clean, flat, dry and structurally sound — a well-bonded ceramic floor with tight grout lines sometimes qualifies. Large-format tile is a different story: the substrate underneath tile with any edge 15 inches or longer can vary no more than 1/8 inch over 10 feet under ANSI A108.02, and an old tile floor with lippage or uneven grout lines almost never meets that on its own.

Tile that sounds hollow when you tap it, or that's tenting at the seams, has already lost its bond to the mortar bed and needs to come out regardless of what goes on top; compounding causes like missing movement joints and a poor original bond are the usual culprits. If you're planning new tile installation or waterproof flooring over a currently sound floor, we check it in person before recommending removal.

sections.h2: What does tile removal cost in Sarasota in 2026?
sections.html:
Removal in Sarasota and Manatee County typically runs $1.75 to $3.25 per square foot for carpet, laminate or a floating floor, and $2.50 to $4.50 per square foot for glued tile with thinset chip-out, in 2026. A 400-square-foot kitchen and dining area with glued ceramic tile usually falls between $1,000 and $1,800 for demo alone, before the new floor goes in. Run your own square footage through the flooring cost calculator for a fast estimate, or get exact numbers at the free estimate. A larger 1,200-square-foot whole first floor of glued tile typically runs $3,000 to $5,400 for removal alone, before leveling or the new material.

Angi's 2026 national figures run $2 to $7 per square foot with a $3.50 average, which is wider than our regional range because it covers markets with very different labor costs. See the tile installation cost guide for how removal fits into a full tile job's budget.

sections.h2: What's under the tile on a Gulf Coast slab?
sections.html:
What we find depends heavily on the house's age. Homes built in the 1960s through 1980s around Sarasota and Bradenton often have terrazzo or the original thin-set ceramic straight on the slab, sometimes with a mortar bed thick enough to add real time and cost to the demo. Newer builds usually have large-format porcelain set in a thin-set mortar with less material to chip out, though that tile is heavier and can take longer to break up in whole pieces. Older vinyl-over-slab layers, if they're still down under a later tile job, bring black cutback mastic that needs its own scraping and solvent step. Terrazzo is a genuine slab finish rather than a tile laid on top of the slab, so removing it usually means grinding rather than chipping, and a fair number of owners choose to grind and polish it back to a wear surface instead of covering it once they see what's underneath a later tile job.

Line items that change a removal quote include the demo type itself, how much thinset or mastic grinding is needed, whether the slab needs a moisture test or leveling afterward, baseboard removal and reinstallation, transition strips, furniture moving, and, in a condo, disposing of an old acoustic underlayment along with the flooring. We itemize each of those separately on the written quote instead of folding them into one number.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit for floor removal in Sarasota County?
sections.html: In Sarasota County, replacing flooring without changing the subfloor structure is treated as cosmetic work and doesn't need a building permit, though it's worth confirming with the county building department for anything unusual about your address. That covers straightforward tile, carpet or laminate removal ahead of a new floor. Read more in our post on permit rules for flooring replacement in Sarasota County; condo buildings are a separate matter, since the association's own approval process usually applies on top of whatever the county requires. That same cosmetic-work reading applies to removal on its own, not just the finished install, so pulling up old tile ahead of a leveling job or a slab moisture test doesn't trigger a separate permit either, as long as nothing structural is touched.

sections.h2: What happens to the slab after the tile comes out?
sections.html: Once tile and thinset are off, we look at the bare slab for two things: moisture and flatness. A slab that's read for years under sealed tile can carry more moisture than a new floor's manufacturer allows, especially for glue-down vinyl or hardwood, so a reading happens before we quote the next product. Grinding away a mortar bed or old thinset rarely leaves a perfectly flat surface either, and low spots or ridges that were hidden under tile become visible once everything is gone. If leveling is needed, our subfloor leveling page covers how self-leveling underlayment gets a slab flat enough for the next floor, including for large-format tile.

sections.h2: How long does removal take, and can we stay in the house?
sections.html: A single room's worth of glued tile, roughly 200 to 300 square feet, usually comes out in a day; a whole-house job with multiple rooms and a thick mortar bed can run two to three days before the crew even starts on the new floor. Most homeowners stay in the house, though the room under demolition is off-limits while the hammer and grinder are running, and closing doors to the rest of the house cuts down on how far dust and noise travel. We schedule removal as its own phase rather than rushing it into the same day as installation, since a rushed demo is where hidden problems like a cracked slab section or old plumbing get missed. A 1980s block home in Gulf Gate with three rooms of glued ceramic is a typical example: two days for demo and a moisture check, a day for any floor repair the slab needs, then installation starts once that prep work is done and signed off. Rental owners on a tight turnover window should plan removal several days ahead of the guest calendar rather than the same week, since a moisture reading or an unexpected repair can add a day the schedule didn't have room for.

faqs.q: How much does tile removal cost in Sarasota?
faqs.a: Glued tile with thinset chip-out runs $2.50 to $4.50 per square foot installed in 2026 in Sarasota and Manatee County; carpet, laminate or a floating floor is $1.75 to $3.25 per square foot. A 400 sq ft kitchen typically falls between $1,000 and $1,800 for demo alone.

faqs.q: Is dustless tile removal actually dust-free?
faqs.a: No demo method is fully dust-free. HEPA vacuum shrouds on the chipping hammer and grinder capture debris at the point of impact and cut airborne dust noticeably, but breaking a mortar bed still throws some dust, so we still seal doorways and run a negative-air machine.

faqs.q: Can you install new flooring over existing tile instead of removing it?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Certain rigid-core vinyl plank products can go over a fully adhered, clean, flat, dry and structurally sound tile floor. Hollow-sounding or tenting tile has already lost its bond and has to come out regardless of what product goes on top.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove flooring in Sarasota County?
faqs.a: Replacing flooring without changing the subfloor structure is treated as cosmetic work in Sarasota County and typically doesn't need a building permit. Condo associations often have their own approval process separate from the county's rules.

faqs.q: What's under old tile in a Sarasota home?
faqs.a: It depends on the era. 1960s-1980s homes often have terrazzo or thin-set ceramic straight on the slab, sometimes on a thick mortar bed; newer builds usually have large-format porcelain in a thinner mortar layer that's faster to remove.

faqs.q: Does the slab need anything done after the tile is out?
faqs.a: Usually a moisture reading and a flatness check. A slab sealed under tile for years can read wetter than a new product's installation guide allows, and grinding off old thinset rarely leaves the surface flat enough for large-format tile or vinyl plank without leveling.
